title: Proclus: The Six Books on the Theology of Plato
author: Proclus, trans. Thomas Taylor
query: Proclus Theology of Plato Thomas Taylor
epithet: The last great pagan summa, in Taylor's English
summary: Proclus's systematic theology of the Platonic gods, translated by Thomas Taylor — the fullest surviving statement of late Neoplatonic metaphysics, and the book through which English readers met Proclus for a century.

title: Select Works of Plotinus
author: Plotinus, trans. Thomas Taylor
query: Select Works of Plotinus Thomas Taylor
epithet: The father of Neoplatonism, first in English
summary: Taylor's selection from the Enneads, the earliest substantial English Plotinus — the treatises on beauty, the intelligible and the One that founded the whole later tradition of Platonic mysticism.

title: Select Works of Porphyry
author: Porphyry, trans. Thomas Taylor
query: Select Works of Porphyry Thomas Taylor abstinence
epithet: On abstinence, the cave, and the sensible soul
summary: Taylor's Porphyry — On Abstinence from Animal Food, the Cave of the Nymphs and the Auxiliaries to the Intelligible — the disciple of Plotinus in the translations that shaped English vegetarianism and allegory alike.

title: The Mystical Hymns of Orpheus
author: trans. Thomas Taylor
query: Mystical Hymns of Orpheus Thomas Taylor
epithet: The Orphic hymns to the powers of the cosmos
summary: Taylor's verse translation of the Orphic Hymns, with his essay on the theology behind them — the ritual poetry of the late-antique mysteries that the Platonists took for the oldest Greek revelation.

title: The Eleusinian and Bacchic Mysteries
author: Thomas Taylor
query: Eleusinian and Bacchic Mysteries Thomas Taylor
epithet: A dissertation on the two great initiations
summary: Taylor's essay reading the Eleusinian and Dionysiac mysteries as a dramatised Platonic doctrine of the soul's descent and return — the text that carried the idea of the mysteries into modern occultism.

title: Sallust On the Gods and the World
author: Sallustius, trans. Thomas Taylor
query: Sallust On the Gods and the World Taylor
epithet: The catechism of the last pagans
summary: The short Neoplatonic creed written in the circle of the Emperor Julian, translated by Taylor with the Pythagoric fragments — a compact statement of the theology the pagan revival died defending.

title: Apollonius of Tyana
author: G. R. S. Mead
query: Apollonius of Tyana Mead 1901
epithet: The pagan holy man measured against the Gospels
summary: Mead's study of the first-century sage and wonder-worker whom late antiquity set beside Christ — a sober theosophical reading of Philostratus's Life and the tradition around it.

title: Simon Magus: An Essay
author: G. R. S. Mead
query: Simon Magus Mead essay
epithet: The arch-heretic reconstructed from his enemies
summary: Mead's attempt to recover the historical Simon Magus and his Gnostic system from the hostile Church Fathers who are almost the only witnesses to it — an early exercise in reading heresiology against the grain.

title: Echoes from the Gnosis
author: G. R. S. Mead
query: Echoes from the Gnosis Mead
epithet: Eleven little books of the inner tradition
summary: Mead's series of slim volumes — the Hymn of the Robe of Glory, the Hymns of Hermes, the Wedding-Song of Wisdom and more — each a short Gnostic or Hermetic text with commentary, meant to carry the gnosis to a wide readership.

title: The Doctrine of the Subtle Body in Western Tradition
author: G. R. S. Mead
query: Doctrine of the Subtle Body Mead
epithet: The radiant vehicle of the soul, traced West
summary: Mead's essay on the 'spirit-body' or radiant vehicle of the soul in Greek, Hermetic and Christian thought — the study that put the phrase 'subtle body' into the modern esoteric vocabulary.

title: The Mysteries of Mithra
author: Franz Cumont
query: Mysteries of Mithra Cumont
epithet: The soldier's mystery cult reconstructed
summary: Cumont's founding reconstruction of the Roman Mithraic mysteries from their monuments — the book that made Mithraism a subject, and whose astral reading of the bull-slaying is still the argument every later scholar answers.

title: Oriental Religions in Roman Paganism
author: Franz Cumont
query: Oriental Religions in Roman Paganism Cumont
epithet: How the East converted the Roman soul
summary: Cumont's account of the cults of Cybele, Isis, Mithra and the Syrian gods that flooded into the Empire — the classic statement of how Eastern mystery-religion prepared the ground the later esoteric traditions grew from.

title: The Life of Apollonius of Tyana
author: Philostratus, trans. F. C. Conybeare
query: Life of Apollonius of Tyana Philostratus Conybeare
epithet: The romance of the wandering Pythagorean sage
summary: Philostratus's third-century life of Apollonius, the wonder-working Pythagorean who travelled from Rome to India — the primary source for the sage, in Conybeare's parallel-text translation.

title: The Metamorphosis, or Golden Ass
author: Apuleius, trans. Thomas Taylor
query: Apuleius Golden Ass Metamorphosis Thomas Taylor
epithet: The novel that ends in the mysteries of Isis
summary: Apuleius's comic novel of a man turned donkey, which closes with the only first-person account of an initiation into the mysteries of Isis to survive from antiquity — in Taylor's philosophical translation.

title: The God of Socrates
author: Apuleius, trans. Thomas Taylor
query: Apuleius God of Socrates daemon Taylor
epithet: The classic ancient treatise on daemons
summary: Apuleius's lecture on the daemons who stand between gods and men, and on the personal daemon of Socrates — the fullest pagan doctrine of intermediary spirits, foundational for later angelology and magic.

title: The True Intellectual System of the Universe
author: Ralph Cudworth
query: True Intellectual System of the Universe Cudworth
epithet: The Cambridge Platonist's war on atheism
summary: Cudworth's vast defence of theism, remembered here for its long, learned reconstruction of ancient pagan theology as a veiled monotheism — a scholarly monument of the prisca theologia after Casaubon had wounded it.

title: The History of Philosophy
author: Thomas Stanley
query: Stanley History of Philosophy Chaldaick
epithet: The first English history of philosophy, with the Chaldaic oracles
summary: Stanley's history of the ancient schools, whose final part — a full account of the 'Chaldaick' philosophy and its oracles — was for centuries the standard English source for the Chaldean Oracles.

title: De rebus sacris et ecclesiasticis exercitationes XVI
author: Isaac Casaubon
query: Casaubon De rebus sacris ecclesiasticis exercitationes
epithet: The book that dated the Hermetica and broke the spell
summary: Casaubon's critique of Baronius, in which the philological demonstration that the Hermetic writings are post-Christian, not primeval Egyptian, quietly ended the Renaissance cult of Hermes Trismegistus.

title: Ancient Fragments
author: Isaac Preston Cory
query: Ancient Fragments Cory Berossus Sanchoniatho
epithet: The salvaged scraps of the lost cosmogonies
summary: Cory's collection of the surviving fragments of Berossus, Sanchoniatho, the Hermetic and Orphic writers and the Chaldean Oracles — the quarry from which nineteenth-century occultism drew its 'ancient wisdom'.

title: The Virgin of the World of Hermes Mercurius Trismegistus
author: trans. Anna Kingsford and Edward Maitland
query: Virgin of the World Hermes Trismegistus Kingsford
epithet: The Kore Kosmou and the sermons of Isis
summary: Kingsford and Maitland's translation of the 'Virgin of the World' (the Kore Kosmou) and other Hermetic fragments — the esoteric Christianity of the Hermetic Society, and a bridge from the corpus to the Golden Dawn.

title: Plotinos: Complete Works
author: Plotinus, trans. Kenneth Sylvan Guthrie
query: Plotinos Complete Works Guthrie
epithet: The first complete English Plotinus
summary: Guthrie's four-volume Plotinos, the first rendering of the whole Enneads into English, arranged chronologically with life and commentary — a labour that made the founder of Neoplatonism fully available at last.
imprint: London: George Bell / Comparative Literature Press, 1918

title: Numenius of Apamea, the Father of Neo-Platonism
author: Kenneth Sylvan Guthrie
query: Numenius of Apamea Guthrie
epithet: The Pythagorean who prepared the way for Plotinus
summary: Guthrie's edition of the fragments of Numenius, the second-century Pythagorean-Platonist who fused Plato with the wisdom of the 'Brahmans, Jews, Magi and Egyptians' and set the stage for Plotinus.

title: Hermetica, vol. I: Introduction, Texts, Translation
author: Walter Scott (ed.)
query: Hermetica Scott volume one introduction texts translation
epithet: The Greek text and the great emendations, vol. I
summary: The first volume of Scott's Hermetica — the Greek and Latin texts of the philosophical corpus with facing translation — famous for the boldness with which the editor rewrote the passages he judged corrupt.

title: The Works of Philo Judaeus
author: Philo of Alexandria, trans. C. D. Yonge
query: Works of Philo Judaeus Yonge
epithet: The Alexandrian who married Moses to Plato
summary: Philo's allegorical readings of the Torah through Greek philosophy, in Yonge's four-volume translation — the Logos theology of first-century Alexandria that fed both Christian and Hermetic thought.

title: Of Isis and Osiris
author: Plutarch, trans. in the Morals
query: Plutarch Isis and Osiris Morals
epithet: The priestly account of the Egyptian mystery
summary: Plutarch's essay on the myth and cult of Isis and Osiris, addressed to a priestess of Delphi — the single richest ancient source on Egyptian religion read through Greek philosophy, and a touchstone of Hermetic Egyptianism.
imprint: in Plutarch's Morals, London: Sampson Low, 1878

title: The Commentaries of Proclus on the Timaeus of Plato
author: Proclus, trans. Thomas Taylor
query: Proclus Commentaries Timaeus Plato Taylor
epithet: The Neoplatonic reading of Plato's cosmology
summary: Proclus's great commentary on the Timaeus, in Taylor's two volumes — the fullest late-antique interpretation of Plato's account of the making of the world, a quarry of Neoplatonic cosmology.

title: The Essays and Hymns of Synesius of Cyrene
author: Synesius, trans. Augustine FitzGerald
query: Essays and Hymns of Synesius of Cyrene FitzGerald
epithet: The philosopher who became a reluctant bishop
summary: The letters, essays and Neoplatonic hymns of Synesius — student of Hypatia, then bishop of Ptolemais — including On Dreams and the defence of a philosophy that would not quite become orthodox.

title: Collectanea Hermetica
author: W. Wynn Westcott (ed.)
query: Collectanea Hermetica Westcott
epithet: The Golden Dawn's shelf of Hermetic classics
summary: Westcott's series of Hermetic and alchemical texts — the Divine Pymander, the Chaldean Oracles, Euphrates, the Aesch Mezareph and more — edited for the students of the Golden Dawn's outer order.

title: The Philosophy of Plotinus
author: William Ralph Inge
query: Philosophy of Plotinus Inge Gifford
epithet: The Gifford Lectures on the last great pagan
summary: Dean Inge's two-volume Gifford Lectures on Plotinus — the study that restored the Enneads to English philosophy as a living mysticism rather than an antiquarian curiosity.

title: The Neo-Platonists: A Study in the History of Hellenism
author: Thomas Whittaker
query: The Neo-Platonists Whittaker Hellenism
epithet: The school from Plotinus to its last masters
summary: Whittaker's connected history of the Neoplatonic school from Plotinus through Porphyry, Iamblichus and Proclus — long the standard English survey of the philosophy that closed antiquity.

title: The Christian Platonists of Alexandria
author: Charles Bigg
query: Christian Platonists of Alexandria Bigg Bampton
epithet: Clement and Origen between two worlds
summary: Bigg's Bampton Lectures on Clement and Origen — the Alexandrian theologians who read the gospel through Plato — the classic account of the meeting of Greek philosophy and early Christianity.

title: Forerunners and Rivals of Christianity
author: Francis Legge
query: Forerunners and Rivals of Christianity Legge
epithet: The religious underworld of the Roman East
summary: Legge's survey of the Gnostic, Hermetic, Mithraic and Manichaean movements that competed with early Christianity — a connected picture of the whole religious ferment of late antiquity.

title: Prolegomena to the Study of Greek Religion
author: Jane Ellen Harrison
query: Prolegomena to the Study of Greek Religion Harrison
epithet: The dark, chthonic underside of Olympus
summary: Harrison's study of the older, chthonic layer of Greek religion beneath the Olympian gods — ritual, purifications and mysteries — the book that reshaped how the ancient sacred was understood.

title: Orpheus
author: G. R. S. Mead
query: Orpheus Mead theosophy 1896
epithet: The Orphic theology as a theosophical system
summary: Mead's reconstruction of Orphic theology and cosmogony as a coherent esoteric system — the mythic Greek revelation the Neoplatonists revered, set out for a theosophical readership.

title: Iamblichus on the Mysteries of the Egyptians, Chaldeans, and Assyrians
author: Iamblichus, trans. Thomas Taylor
query: Iamblichus on the Mysteries Egyptians Chaldeans Taylor 1821
epithet: The great defence of theurgy, Taylor's first edition
summary: Iamblichus's answer to Porphyry — the classic ancient defence of theurgy, the ritual working with the gods — in Taylor's translation, the text through which the West recovered the practice of Neoplatonic magic.
